extracted.intended_audience: military pay officers, paymasters, quartermasters, legal officers, and War Department accountants
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative and legal standards governing entitlement, computation, withholding, forfeiture, and special allowances (heat/light, quarters, forage, extra-duty pay, clothing, rations, transportation, etc.) for officers and enlisted men in the U.S. Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat and light — general entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat and light furnished only to buildings used by officer or enlisted man at his post of duty; no limit fixed on cost to Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right accrues after assignment to quarters or allowance of commutation; heat and light is an allowance in kind and cannot be commuted into money; officer drawing commutation of quarters does not lose right to heat and light for temporary absence in hospital for treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat and light — officers' specific rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for officers: chiefs and assistant chiefs of Constabulary entitled on their actual rank only; right to increased allowance accrues at date of promotion; an officer who retains quarters at a post or draws commutation of quarters while on leave of absence is entitled to his allowance of heat and light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of status and timing (e.g., promotion date) determine increased allowance; temporary absences do not necessarily suspend entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat and light — enlisted men rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In leasing quarters for enlisted men, leases should stipulate that heat and light will be furnished; right to heat and light not affected because enlisted man draws commutation of quarters; enlisted men living outside of reservation not entitled to heat and light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heat and light should not be sold to others than officers and enlisted men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation allowances for officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowances for transportation of officer himself, of horse, and of baggage are recognized; reimbursements for horse when changing station and from other places than last station; baggage treatment governed by Army Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Mileage in Pay Manual and Transportation of the Army — Baggage; reimbursements follow statutory/Regulation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarters allowance and commutation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commutation of quarters is recognized; use of quarters by officer's family while officer is on duty that carries commutation is permitted; rules apply for quarters when traveling on duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to Army Regulations for procedural details; commutation interacts with other allowances (heat and light).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interment expense allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Interment expenses allowed in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not allowed if officer on sick leave; temporary interment does not preclude permanent interment elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage allowance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Forage allowance payable only where a horse is owned and actually kept; fictitious assumption of ownership does not create right to forage; duty must require a mount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act of May 11, 1908 does not change the requirement that the horse be actually owned and kept; duty test (performance of duty requiring mounted status) controls entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing allowance for enlisted men
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothing allowance is not part of pay and has special rules regarding forfeiture and issue in kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clothing not credited when pay is not [text truncated]; clothing issued in kind does not become private property; clothing allowance may be forfeited by sentence of court-martial; gratuitous issues may be made to replace clothing destroyed in campaign, by fire, or to prevent contagion; dishonorably discharged soldier not authorized gratuitous issue unless sentenced to confinement; soldier discharged without honor for fraudulent enlistment may forfeit clothing allowance on discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rations and commutation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rations and their commutation are subject to rates fixed by the Secretary of War and special rules when traveling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutation rates fixed by the Secretary of War; when traveling, commutation limited to the trip; see Army Regulations and Subsistence Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprivation of pay and allowances — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer or soldier can only be deprived of legal pay while in the military establishment by a duly adjudged and approved sentence of court-martial, by operation of law under express statutory enactment, or under Army regulations; pay cannot be deprived by summary dismissal or by implication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being under charges, in arrest, or awaiting sentence does not, except as provided by regulation, affect right to regular pay of rank; legal deprivation requires due process or express statutory/regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stoppage of pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Stoppage may occur in connection with arrest as deserter; may be collected in monthly amounts; overpayments to employees may be stopped against the disbursing officer; stoppage cannot be made to satisfy private claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stoppage is a 'charge on account' to make good a loss; cannot be made to reimburse a personal indebtedness which grows out of an incorrect final statement; may be made to reimburse company fund, even in paying account of deceased officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of pay by court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Forfeiture of pay and allowances may be imposed by sentence of court-martial: of pay earned, of pay due and to become due, and of 'all pay and allowances' for a certain period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeiture of pay earned applies if sentenced to dishonorable discharge; forfeiture may include commutation of quarters, fuel, and rations; necessary clothing and subsistence may still be issued even when all pay and allowances are forfeited for a period; destruction of record before approval nullifies forfeitures; forfeited money returns to the Treasury and credited to Army pay; some forfeitures apply only to the current enlistment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeitures otherwise than by sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain forfeitures occur by operation of law or status: clothing allowance on discharge without honor for fraudulent enlistment; pay and allowances while absent without leave; travel allowances in certain dishonorable discharges; public property lost charged to soldier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various categories of non-court-martial forfeiture are enumerated and applied depending on discharge status and circumstances of absence or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fines
rubrics_metrics.description: Fines accrue only by sentence of court-martial and accrue to the United States; fines are distinct from stoppage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fines must be imposed by proper judicial process and are credited to the United States rather than withheld for other private claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remission of forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Remission of forfeiture operates only on pay not due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remission does not operate retroactively to pay already due or paid; procedural limits apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation rule for dismissal-to-suspension of cadet
rubrics_metrics.description: Commutation on dismissal of cadet to suspension does not forfeit pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific status changes (dismissal to suspension) have prescribed pay consequences; consult cited decisions/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to pay — start and end of entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to pay begins and ends with the period of legal service; except by special authority of Congress, cannot be paid for service rendered before appointment, enlistment, or muster in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a soldier is detained beyond enlistment term by accident or exigency of service, he is entitled to pay for such additional period; an officer separated by dismissal/retirement/resignation is entitled to pay up to the day he personally receives official notice of the detaching order; cannot be dismissed/discharged/mustered out with a prior date that deprives him of pay accrued between that prior date and actual discharge without authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay accrual on appointment or promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: In original appointment, pay begins from date of acceptance; in promotion, from date of vacancy; Congress may authorize appointment with rank back-dated, but without specific authority back pay is not granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance may be implied by entry upon duties; authorities and case law cited (Dig. Comp. Dec., U.S. v. Eaton, etc.) govern nuances; Pay Manual references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status while awaiting orders or on 'waiting orders'
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer ordered home to await orders does not occupy status of officer on leave of absence and is not on half pay; he is entitled to full pay of his rank while awaiting orders when ordered by Secretary of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court and departmental decisions cited where awaiting orders did or did not confer leave status; check specific facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay accounts and negotiability/assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer's pay account is not commercial paper but a mere receipt; assignment/transfer of pay accounts is permitted when due and payable under act of Mar. 2, 1907 but drawing checks to indorsees may violate statute (sec. 3620 R.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bona fide assignee delivering account with name written on back does not incur indorser liability; practice of drawing checks to order of indorsee may violate law; comptroller and Attorney General opinions cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment to guardian/committee for incapacitated officers
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer declared non compos mentis, the War Department will recognize guardian/committee appointed by civil authorities and pay salary to such guardian/committee on proper representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal representation and appointment required; Comptroller decisions cited (C. 29315, Dec. 12, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting service for longevity and continuous service
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain services (e.g., service as a medical cadet) may be counted for longevity pay; continuous-service time excludes absence without leave; dishonorable discharge prevents counting prior service for continuous-service pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory sections and Pay Manual references govern computation; where facts are not fully set forth on muster rolls, obtain records from The Adjutant General; examples and Comptroller/Attorney General decisions cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra-duty pay — eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra-duty pay covers only labor legitimately performed in the military service by soldiers as such; not payable for private employment; extra-duty pay is payable only for 'constant labor for a period of not less than ten days'; rates specified by statute/appropriation for mechanics, artisans, school-teachers, clerks, and other enlisted men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: single-day services (auctioneer) do not qualify; detail to civilian telegraph company not qualifying; staff-department service generally excluded unless service rendered in another department unrelated to normal duties; cooks and certain enlisted categories have distinct rules; extra-duty pay may be drawn from particular appropriations or from receipts of post funds where authorized; wartime statutes may bar additional extra-duty pay (act of April 26, 1898) except from certain funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation-source rules for extra-duty pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriations are made for work other than extra-duty items, enlisted men may be employed on that work and paid extra compensation from that appropriation under proper restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra-duty pay might be paid to printers out of the printing appropriation or to workers constructing a target range from funds set aside for that construction; must conform to restrictions and proper authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposits for purchase of discharge — forfeiture on desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier's deposit (e.g., $50 under act of May 15, 1872) in anticipation of application for purchase of discharge is unconditional; if soldier deserts while application pending, the deposit is forfeited like any other deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller and case decisions cited (C. 807, Jan. 1895; 14901, July/Aug. 1903; 17311, Jan. 1905).
